data.title: Hallador Energy wins Indiana regulatory OK for 12-year capacity sale expected to generate $1B
data.description:
Hallador Energy (HNRG) rose 3.6% post-market Thursday after saying the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission approved a 12-year capacity agreement with an unnamed utility company, satisfying the regulatory approval condition to the agreement, which is now effective.

Hallador (HNRG) said the deal is expected to generate more than $1B in capacity revenue from its Merom Generating Station through mid-2040, at a fixed price that substantially exceeds its historical capacity pricing.

Deliveries begin with a smaller volume of accredited capacity in late 2028, rising to roughly two-thirds of Hallador's (HNRG) accredited capacity beginning in 2029 and continuing through the end of the 12-year term, the company said.

"We've put long-term contracts in place and made significant progress on our plans to grow our power business," Hallador (HNRG) President and CEO Brent Bilsland said. "This approval demonstrates that Indiana's regulators are still supporting the growth of data centers in Indiana."

data.title: Curtiss-Wright boosts 2026 buyback program by $250M
data.description:
• Curtiss-Wright (CW) announced on Thursday a $250M increase to its 2026 share repurchase program, bringing expected annual buybacks to a record $710M.

  • The company also declared a quarterly dividend of $0.26 per share, payable December 11 to shareholders of record on November 27.

  • It authorized an additional $60M in share repurchases beginning in January 2027 to offset potential dilution from employee compensation plans.

  • CEO Lynn Bamford said the expanded buyback reflects confidence in the company's financial outlook and long-term growth strategy.

data.title: Anthropic founders and employers worth more than a third of US households
data.description:
Anthropic’s (ANT) founders and employers are worth more than the bottom third of the U.S. households.

According to data from the Anthropic prospectus as of Nov. 19 and the Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances of 2025, the AI startup’s 5,300 founders and employers are worth $433B.

The seven co-founders are now worth $163B, and the rest of the employees are worth $270B, as the company closed $97.17, up more than 17% from its IPO initial trading price.

The bottom third of the U.S. households, accounting for more than 45M households, are worth $432B.

data.title: Bending Spoons rallies 7% after the close on Mailchimp deal
data.description:
Bending Spoons (BSP) shares rose more than 7% after the closing bell following the announcement of a deal to acquire Mailchimp for ~$3.68B. The consideration consists of $3.31B in cash and $368M in Bending Spoons' stock.

This followed a 3% dip during the session, with the stock finished at $41.70, down $1.09 on the day.

In addition, the digital-business acquirer said it agreed to sell 32.5 million ordinary shares in the private placement, with closing expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. Trading volume reached 4.26 million shares, and relative volume stood at 2.17.

data.title: Warby Parker sinks 14% as choppy trading continues
data.description:
Eyewear company Warby Parker (WRBY) dropped more than 14% on Wednesday. The stock finished at $24.13, falling $4.09 on the day.

The decline came as the broader market also fell. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF slipped almost 2%, and the consumer discretionary sector ETF lost almost 3%.

WRBY has seen choppy trading lately. The stock climbed nearly 9% on Wednesday following two straight days of losses. Shares also saw a drop of 11% on November 12, coming shortly after a rally of 19% on November 9.
